features.label: Need a thing; relative complement
features.description: Beðurfan takes a genitive of the thing needed in the selected ordinary frame, e.g. hwǣtes. In ðā ðing ðe wē beðurfon, ðā ðing is accusative object of buy, while invariant ðe supplies the dependency required by beðurfan within the relative. Its unchanged spelling does not make the internal dependency accusative. BT95 directly quotes this very Genesis43.4/8 clause; it also attests other government, so accusative alternatives are not globally impossible.
features.scope_limitation: Only the stated elementary frame is assigned; forms, senses and other constructions retain their separate status.

features.label: Recognize an accusative person
features.description: Oncnāwan in the selected recognition sense takes an accusative recognized person. The nominative recognizer controls the verb; a change of recognizer from ic to wē changes person/number independently of the object. Present cnāw-/cnǣw- and past cnēow- stay distinct.
features.scope_limitation: Only the stated elementary frame is assigned; forms, senses and other constructions retain their separate status.

features.label: Open an accusative container
features.description: Undōn means undo/open the tied sacks in45.8 and takes the accusative container. Present dēð and preterite dyde are different stems; plural preterite undydon follows the plural opener, not the number of sacks.
features.scope_limitation: Only the stated elementary frame is assigned; forms, senses and other constructions retain their separate status.

features.label: Swear oaths and report their content
features.description: Swęrian/swerian takes accusative āðas as the sworn utterance. A dative recipient mīnum fæder48.1 needs no English to; ætforan us44.2 names the people in whose presence it was sworn. The reported content is a ðæt clause: mōsten gives past reported permission, brōhte a promised bringing viewed prospectively from the former oath. The two case frames are not interchangeable.

prior_records.description: Swęrian with ðurh+accusative names the oath standard. Repeated ne ðurh phrases share the initial negative command.

features.scope_limitation: Only the stated elementary frame is assigned; forms, senses and other constructions retain their separate status.

features.label: Desire that a state of affairs occur
features.description: 44.5 retains the explicitly required genitive demonstrative ðæs after giernan, followed by the content-explaining ðæt clause. Lǣdden is first-plural past subjunctive under the former desire; the second ðæt is a conjunction, not a second case-inflected demonstrative. The earlier genitive thing/person request frame alone did not teach this full propositional use.

prior_records.description: Giernan governs the desired/requested thing or marriage partner in the genitive. Æt+dative identifies the person asked in39.3. The invariant relative ðe avoids demanding productive relative case attraction; the main-clause eall ðæt retains its own accusative object role.43.14’s genitive maiden is a marriage request, not a direct-object accusative.

features.label: Make a person be gracious
features.description: Gedōn has accusative person hine plus agreeing accusative masculine singular glædne. In45.2 gedō is third-singular present subjunctive expressing the wish; it is not an imperative addressed to the named Lord. Wið ēow supplies the graciousness target, as the original hint expressly requires.
features.scope_limitation: Only the stated elementary frame is assigned; forms, senses and other constructions retain their separate status.

features.label: Give back a person
features.description: Āgiefan selects the returned person as accusative and the recipient as dative. Ēow and ēowerne brōðor have different roles. Present subjunctive āgiefe is in the final purpose clause, not merely an unexplained alternative ending.
features.scope_limitation: Only the stated elementary frame is assigned; forms, senses and other constructions retain their separate status.

features.label: Despoil someone of possessions
features.description: Berēafian takes accusative person and genitive possessions in its selected active frame. In the passive the deprived person becomes the nominative subject, while genitive mīnra bearna remains.45.6 has genitive plural assena and ðinga; selfe agrees with accusative ūs in the following enslavement clause. BT Supplement81 gives this genitive construction and separately documents instrumental/dative alternatives, which must not be mislabeled impossible.

features.label: Listen to speech
features.description: Hlystan governs genitive speech/content in45.7, as the explicit156 hint directs. Thus ūrre sprǣce is genitive feminine singular, distinct from accusative ūre sprǣce. The people beseech the steward (ðē accusative); ðū is the subject of subordinate hlyste.

features.label: Enslave an accusative person
features.description: The selected ðēowian sense is enslave, with an accusative person. BT1056 senseII cites precisely Gen43.18, ðæt hē ūs ðēowige. The more common serve sense with different government remains separate. Our ðēowie normalizes the documented -ige/-ie variation under Cook119 and does not change tense or mood.

features.label: Command a dative person
features.description: Bēodan takes a dative addressee in46.7 and48.8, as164 expressly directs. It can accompany a direct command or introduce ðæt plus subjunctive commanded action.47.11 intentionally retains present bīetst (commandest); the lookalike bīetst of bēatan is not the lexical identity here.

features.label: Lay out things
features.description: Lęcgean takes accusative things laid, with forð marking their presentation in46.3. Its source reading imperative lęcgeað is separately supplied; learning indicative plural lęcgeað does not by itself assign the command use.

features.label: Mention a person earlier to someone
features.description: Foresęcgean here means mention previously, not foretell the future. The invariant ðe is the mentioned person (accusative function), and mē the dative hearer. The English of is explicitly omitted. BT Supplement240 distinguishes the past-reference sense and illustrates a person mentioned earlier.

features.label: Be grieved by a stated circumstance
features.description: Ofðyncean is third-singular impersonal with dative experiencer ēow and a cause/content ðæt clause. Present subjunctive ofðynce gives nor let it grieve you; no separately invented personal subject it is needed. The plural experiencer does not demand a plural verb. The four-cell paradigm explicitly limits productive morphology to this impersonal construction.
features.scope_limitation: Only the stated elementary frame is assigned; forms, senses and other constructions retain their separate status.

features.label: Fear with genitive object and reflexive dative
features.description: 48.6 extends the previously taught accusative feared-entity frame to the directly attested genitive frame: reflexive dative ēow plus nānes ðinges. Cook156h/159a explicitly gives ne ondrǣd ðū ðē ǣniges ðinges.46.1 has only the reflexive dative, with no expressed feared entity. This ēow is not an accusative object merely because its spelling is syncretic.

features.label: Requite good with evil
features.description: In46.9 accusative neuter gōd is the good being repaid; mid yfele is the evil given in return. The recipient frame previously used for paying is not by itself this good-for-evil substitution frame. Wolden is third-plural past subjunctive inside the reported why-question; forgieldan is its plain infinitive.

features.label: Prospective when with subjunctive
features.description: 46.9 when you have caught them concerns a future condition for the command to ask. The selected ðonne ðū hīe fō uses second-singular present subjunctive, following196b. There is no required present-perfect auxiliary. Original English says you, and the singular steward continues as addressee of Ārīs, gā and āsca.

features.label: Subjunctive within an optative relative
features.description: 47.3 retains195: in sīe hē ofslægen mid ðǣm ðe ðū hit finde, finde is second-singular present subjunctive within the relative governed by the hypothetical/optative context. Mid takes a dative associate; ðe is invariant. This is not a rule that every relative clause uses subjunctive.

features.label: Narrative preterite with anterior meaning
features.description: Cook188 permits the simple preterite for English simple, perfect and pluperfect past. In45.8 cēapodon and ǣr sealdon give the anterior actions;46.9 fōron ... sumne dǣl ðæs weges conveys had gone without an unassigned intransitive habban perfect. Each clause remains present in the model.

prior_records.description: A simple preterite can express action earlier than another past viewpoint.

Cook188 expressly permits the simple preterite for all three past tenses. Thus37.6 first sętte, and40.4/6–8 simple preterites, can represent the English perfect without inventing new auxiliary-plus-participle cells. Analytic habban perfect is a defensible alternative where the precise participle is actually taught or supplied. An om.hath control reinforces a target; its absence is not a command to calque every English perfect.

features.label: Conceal oneself
features.description: Diernan takes the concealed person as accusative; hine in48.4 refers back to nominative Iosep. Meahte is past ability and governs the plain infinitive. Longer is an adverb modifying concealment, not an adjective agreeing with Joseph.

whole_frame_support.whole_frame_analysis: Complete contrary condition and anterior result: if this delay were not, we would already have come a second time. Nǣre is ne+wǣre, third-singular past subjunctive; wǣren is first-plural past subjunctive. Cumen is a past participle with intransitive wesan, not the identically spelled present-subjunctive plural. Ōðre sīðe is adverbial instrumental singular, expressly176; the sīð hint names the lemma and does not suppress its ending. The entire combined construction and contracted form are supplied; no general counterfactual-perfect mastery is inferred.

whole_frame_support.support_span: Nū twā gēar hunger wæs ofer ealle eorðan, and gīet sculon fīf, on ðǣm mann nāhwæðer ne ęrian ne rīpan mæg
whole_frame_support.whole_frame_analysis: Two years is accusative duration; singular hunger governs wæs. Ofer takes accusative extent ealle eorðan, as172 requires. Fīf stands for five further years; the source explicitly omits there and be, so sculon has an understood existential complement, not a missing translation item. On ðǣm refers to those years. Indefinite mann is singular subject of mæg; nāhwæðer plus ne...ne excludes both infinitive activities. Cook89a supplies the full pronoun; BT Supplement646 independently attests the equivalent contracted nāðer with paired negated infinitives under mihte. All ellipsis, future use and negative coordination are supplied together.
